subject: Dedicated capacity: SKU alignment and latency boundary for Velaris
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@velaris.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-18 09:12 -0700
Subject: Velaris long-context / batch profile + capacity ask

Hi team,

Thanks for the run earlier — attaching the producer-side profile and a short note on SLAs. TL;DR: our product has two main traffic patterns:
- Live chat: low latency requirement (~150–250ms p50 on generation), high concurrency but short context (~1k tokens).
- Document ingestion + batch answers: very long context (up to 800k tokens pre-chunking), latency can be relaxed (1–10s), but memory headroom is critical for single-job runs.

We want a Dedicated plan (reserved capacity) with predictable cost and a clear fallthrough strategy for peaks. Key asks:
1) SKU guidance — do we reserve H100s for the long-context ingestion jobs and use L4/A100 for live traffic?
2) Burst plan — what do we do when reserved slots are saturated?
3) Can you confirm expected p50 token latency for both SKUs under our workload?

Attached: velaris_workload_profile_v2.csv (sample traces), brief cost sensitivity note.

Sam
Head of Platform
Velaris Systems

Attachment: velaris_workload_profile_v2.csv (text/csv, 120KB)
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@velaris.ai>, irene_choi@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-18 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Velaris long-context / batch profile + capacity ask

Sam — thanks for the profile. Quick operational read and draft proposal below. I ran microbenchmarks against sample traces (attached matrix pdf) and summarized practical tradeoffs.

Short summary (recommendation):
- H100: primary reserved SKU for document-ingest/long-context batches. Rationale: larger HBM and better single-job throughput for heavy KV cache and long attention windows; fewer OOMs when pinning >100GB working set.
- A100: mid-tier reserved fallback for mixed workloads. Good for stacked shorter long-context windows when cost sensitivity matters.
- L4: best-effort reserved for live chat (short context). Very cost efficient for many concurrent low-memory requests; significantly cheaper tokens/dollar.

Operational notes / canary & fallthrough:
- Reserve a hybrid pool: 40% H100, 40% A100, 20% L4 initially. We should size slots to hit your p50 latency SLOs (150–250ms live; <3s batch p50 for typical chunks).
- Use prefix KV caching for live chat to keep p50 low on L4; route long-context jobs to H100 with pre-warmed KV cache and increased concurrency limits.
- Burst: allow cross-SKU fallthrough to committed A100 or hosted instances when H100 pool is saturated; define overflow throttles per route so live chat never competes with batch windows.

Cost/throughput heuristics (from our bench):
- H100: best single-job throughput for sequences >64k tokens, 2–3x A100 on memory-heavy stretch; per-token cost ~1.8x A100 in reserved pricing, but reduces retries/engineered chunking effort.
- A100: solid generalist, better tokens/$ than H100 for mid-length contexts.
- L4: ~0.35x A100 tokens/$ for short-chat; not suitable for >64k single jobs without external sharding.

Open asks for Velaris ops team:
- Confirm SLA priority between live chat and ingestion windows — we need to lock routing priority so ops can automate fallthrough.
- Any fixed date for reserve commitment? Pricing/commit levels change if they commit 12+ months.

I attached the SKU recommendation matrix (sku_recommendation_matrix_v1.pdf) with measurement charts and slotting math.

Diego
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachment: sku_recommendation_matrix_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 2.1MB)
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@velaris.ai>
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-18 13:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Velaris long-context / batch profile + capacity ask

Sam — appreciate the detailed traces and Diego's fast benchmarking. I want to align on a pragmatic committed SKU plan that balances your cost targets and our operational guardrails. Proposed next steps and decision points below.

Decision recommendation (we'll finalize after your confirmation):
1) Reserved pool mix (initial, adjustable after 30d telemetry): H100 35% | A100 45% | L4 20%.
2) Slot sizing: provision H100 nodes in 1.5x headroom for your peak long-context ingestion windows (accounts for caching warmup and egress spikes).
3) Routing policy: give live chat strict priority routing to L4/A100 with hard caps on batch concurrency; batch jobs routed to H100 with a queued retry policy and soft preemption after 30s for live-critical requests.
4) Burst policy: when H100 reserved slots are exhausted, overflow to A100 reserve first, then to our hosted (autoscale) pool; define a credit-based fallback to avoid surprise cost exposure.

Commercial note: if Velaris signs a 12-month reserved commitment at the proposed mix, I can secure a blended reserved rate that narrows the H100/A100 premium differential and includes one emergency credit allowance for a production incident during the first 90 days.

Please confirm: (A) SLA priority mapping above, (B) willingness to start with a 12-month commit (we'll model 6/12/24 options), and (C) how many parallel long-context ingestion jobs you expect at peak (Diego's slot math assumes 6 concurrent long ingestion jobs).

If you approve, I'll prepare the formal capacity term sheet and run a quick canary deployment plan with your SREs next week.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Dedicated Solutions | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com, Sam Carter <sam.carter@velaris.ai>
Date: 2027-08-18 16:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Velaris long-context / batch profile + capacity ask

+1 to Irene's recommendation. Two operational caveats:
- We'll need a runbook for preemption so batch jobs can be checkpointed/resumed; Diego can draft that and attach to the term sheet.
- Networking: Velaris said they will use VPC peering; their egress patterns look spiky during ingestion — Ops wants a runway to tune circuit breakers.

Sam — if you confirm (A) and (C) above by EOD Thursday, we'll lock pricing options and Irenes' credit allowance in the reserve proposal draft.

Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Ops | Redwood Inference
